import dlt
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, trim, to_date
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.getActiveSession()
catalog = spark.conf.get("catalog")
target_schema = spark.conf.get("target_schema")  # silver target schema, e.g., consumer_order_silver
# Derive bronze schema from silver target
bronze_schema = target_schema.replace("_silver", "_bronze")
bronze_table = f"{catalog}.{bronze_schema}.consumer_order_mv"
# Parent consumer table for referential integrity check
parent_schema = target_schema.replace("_order_silver", "_silver")  # consumer_order_silver -> consumer_silver
parent_table = f"{catalog}.{parent_schema}.consumer_mv"

@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_fk_consumer_order_to_consumer", "parent_consumer_id IS NOT NULL")
@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_order_id", "order_id IS NOT NULL")
@dlt.table(
    name="consumer_order_mv",
    comment="Silver consumer_order view with cleaned data",
    table_properties={"quality": "silver"},
    schema="""
        order_id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
        consumer_id INT,
        order_date DATE,
        order_status STRING,
        total_amount DOUBLE,
        currency STRING,
        payment_method STRING,
        channel STRING,
        billing_address STRING,
        shipping_address STRING
    """
)
def consumer_order_mv():
    # Read from bronze table as a batch source
    df = spark.read.table(bronze_table)
    # Trim whitespace from string columns
    string_cols = ["order_status", "currency", "payment_method", "channel", "billing_address", "shipping_address"]
    for c in string_cols:
        df = df.withColumn(c, trim(col(c)))
    # Convert order_date to date type
    df = df.withColumn("order_date", to_date(col("order_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))
    # Referential integrity check: validate consumer_id references consumer.consumer_mv
    parent_df = spark.read.table(parent_table).select(col("consumer_id").alias("parent_consumer_id"))
    df = df.join(parent_df, df["consumer_id"] == parent_df["parent_consumer_id"], "left")
    return df
